title: AI Fails to Deliver a 4-Day Work Week - Especially at AI Companies - Slashdot

content_html:
"An engineering director at Google said four years ago that AI would deliver a four-day work week by 2025," remembers the BBC. And earlier this year OpenAI "formally urged companies to start testing out a four-day work week (with no change in pay), claiming that AI will soon be able to speed up so much human labour that the corporate world should prepare itself." However, a former OpenAI technical employee who left the company last year told the BBC the firm never actually trialled the four-day work week it suggested others should try while they were there. Instead, the person described what was often a gruelling work culture marked by frequent "crisis meetings", working on weekends, and "super cut-throat" performance reviews that would see colleagues suddenly let go... [T]he former OpenAI employee said they would put in at least 70 hours a week, much more than they did in previous tech jobs...

Other companies have also pushed the idea that AI will effectively reduce the number of hours people need to work, for better or worse. [At OpenAI and Anthropic] sprints can stretch on for many weeks and top 90 hours of work in a seven-day period, tech workers that the BBC spoke to for this story said... At Meta, workers said they have been abruptly pushed onto teams this year doing AI work being treated as urgent... The hours on such teams at Meta are often long, with staff working into the night, on weekends, and feeling they are "on call" during the hours they are not working, according to descriptions of the work from the current and former employees...

Some new research suggests that AI tools are making people's workloads even more burdensome. A study out of UC Berkeley followed hundreds of workers at a US tech company for eight months as they used AI. It found the employees "worked at a faster pace, took on a broader scope of tasks, and extended work into more hours of the day"... The UC Berkeley research found that the workload of tech employees was expanded in part because of the need to constantly check the output of AI tools.


In the article Neil Thompson, an innovation scholar at MIT, pointed out a problem with estimates that AI will ease the workload on humans. "People assume that 20% less work means four-day weeks. But new work emerges."

The BBC also points out helpfully that "there are no limits in the U.S. on how many hours a person over the age of 16 can work." (While in the UK and Europe, "laws limit a working week to 48 hours, including overtime.")

Thanks to long-time Slashdot reader hadleyburg for sharing the article.

content_html_zh:
“谷歌的一位工程总监四年前曾表示，到 2025 年，人工智能将实现每周工作四天”，BBC 回忆道。 今年早些时候，OpenAI“正式敦促企业开始测试每周工作四天（薪资不变），声称人工智能很快就能加快人力劳动速度，企业界应该做好准备。” 然而，一位去年离开该公司的前 OpenAI 技术员工告诉 BBC，该公司从未真正尝试过它建议其他人在公司工作时应该尝试的四天工作周。 相反，该人士描述了一种艰苦的工作文化，其特点是频繁的“危机会议”、周末工作以及“超级残酷”的绩效评估，导致同事突然解雇……前 OpenAI 员工表示，他们每周至少投入 70 个小时，比以前的技术工作要多得多…… 其他公司也提出这样的想法：人工智能将有效减少人们需要工作的时间，无论好坏。 BBC 为本文采访的技术人员表示，[OpenAI 和 Anthropic] 冲刺可以持续数周，并且在 7 天内可以完成 90 小时的工作…… 在 Meta，工人们表示，他们今年突然被推入团队，从事人工智能工作，并被视为紧急...... 根据现任和前任员工对工作的描述，Meta 此类团队的工作时间通常很长，员工在周末加班到深夜，在不工作的时间里感觉自己“随叫随到”…… 一些新的研究表明，人工智能工具正在使人们的工作负担变得更加繁重。 加州大学伯克利分校的一项研究对一家美国科技公司的数百名员工使用人工智能进行了为期八个月的跟踪。 调查发现，员工“工作节奏更快，承担的任务范围更广，工作时间更长”…… 加州大学伯克利分校的研究发现，技术员工的工作量增加的部分原因是需要不断检查人工智能工具的输出。 麻省理工学院创新学者尼尔·汤普森在文章中指出了人工智能将减轻人类工作量的估计存在问题。 “人们认为工作量减少 20% 意味着每周工作四天。 但新的工作出现了。”

BBC 还指出，“在美国，16 岁以上的人可以工作多少小时没有限制。” （而在英国和欧洲，“法律将每周工作时间限制为 48 小时，包括加班时间。”）

感谢 Slashdot 的长期读者 hadleyburg 分享这篇文章。
